sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 1.1.15 and its proof, pp.11–12, in the author PDF https://math.berkeley.edu/~swshin/HT.pdf (41 pp., created 27 January 2021, SHA-256 fd22990b…52db), the latest version found; the published text, Duke Math. sourceIssues.printed: "Corollary 1.1.15. Let G be an arbitrary connected reductive group over Q_p with a Q_p-rational Levi subgroup M. Let μ: G_m → M be a minuscule cocharacter and [b_M] ∈ B(M)_b such that ([b_M], {μ}) is G-admissible. Then there exists w ∈ W(G, M) := N_G(M)/M such that ([b_M], {w·μ}) is M-admissible." Proof: "(1.1.13) implies that there exists w* ∈ W(G*, M*) such that ([b_{M*}], {w*·μ*}) is M*-admissible."
sourceIssues.correction: Replace N_G(M)/M by the absolute Weyl group W(G, T) of a maximal torus T ⊂ M with μ ∈ X_*(T), as in Proposition 1.1.13. Equivalently: some G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ′ of μ factoring through T makes ([b_M], {μ′}) M-admissible.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed statement fails already for split G. Take G = GL_3, M = GL_1 × GL_2 (blocks of sizes 1 and 2), μ = (0,1,0) and b_M = diag(p,1,1), which is basic in M. Then ([b_M], {μ}) is G-admissible: its Newton point (1,0,0) equals the dominant μ̄, and both have κ_G = 1. But κ_M(b_M) = (1,0), while κ_M(μ) = (0,1). Since the blocks have different sizes, N_G(M) = M, so W(G, M) is trivial and no w in it helps. The permutation of the first two coordinates, in W(G, T) = S_3, does. The proof transports to the quasi-split inner form and applies Proposition 1.1.13. That proposition gives w* in the absolute Weyl group W(G*, T*), not in N_{G*}(M*)/M*, so the proof establishes the corrected statement. The only use is in the proof of Corollary 1.1.17, p.13, for G not necessarily quasi-split. It cites "Lemma 1.1.13" (the quasi-split Proposition 1.1.13) in the form w ∈ W(G, T). The corrected Corollary 1.1.15 is exactly what that step needs, so the later results stand. Checked on the page images. Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 2, items N29 and N32), which also verified the Weyl-group computation by machine.

sourceIssues.printed: "Proposition 1.2.5. Let [b] ∈ B(G_{Q_p}) be a class such that ([b], {μ_X^{−1}}_p) is admissible. Assume hypothesis (1.1.3.1) holds for [b]. Then there exist a maximal torus T ⊂ G and an element x ∈ X with h_x factoring through T_R (in which case μ_x^{−1} ∈ X_*(T)) such that [b_bas(μ_x)] ∈ B(T_{Q_p}) maps to [b] ∈ B(G_{Q_p})."
sourceIssues.reason: The hypothesis concerns {μ_X^{−1}}, and the parenthesis introduces μ_x^{−1} ∈ X_*(T). The proof ends with "[b_bas(μ_T^{−1})] maps to [b]" and uses [b_bas(μ_p^{−1})] throughout. The classes of μ_x and μ_x^{−1} differ, as κ_T already shows for T = G_m. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 3, item G08).

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.2.8, p.28, in the author PDF https://math.berkeley.edu/~swshin/HT.pdf (41 pp., created 27 January 2021, SHA-256 fd22990b…52db), the latest version found; the published text, Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), 1559–1614, was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "Let G′ = G × T, equipped with the symplectic representation V′ = V ⊕ V. Let X′ = X × {h_T}. Then we have (G′, X′) ↪ (G_{V′}, H_{V′}). … Restricting the action of I_{s′_0} to A_T induces a map of Q-groups I_{s′_0} → T, and we consider the composite I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab. By Corollary 2.1.9, I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0} is surjective, so the map I_{s′_0} → G^ab factors through I_{s_0}, as this is true over Q_ℓ for any ℓ ≠ p."
sourceIssues.correction: Take G′ = G ×_{G^ab} T, the pairs (g, t) with the same image in G^ab. This lies in GSp(V ⊕ V, ψ ⊕ ψ), and X′ = X × {h_T} still maps into it because h^ab is constant on X. The kernel of G′ → G is T ∩ G^der, which dies in G^ab, so the composite I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab does factor through I_{s_0}. The rest of the proof then goes through.
sourceIssues.reason: Read literally, the construction fails at two points. First, G × T acting on V ⊕ V does not preserve ψ ⊕ ψ up to a scalar when the similitude factors of g and t differ, so it is not a subgroup of G_{V′}. Second, the claimed factorization fails. The CM automorphisms (1, t), t ∈ T, act trivially on A_{s_0} and by t on A_T, and they preserve the tensors cutting out G × T. So 1 × T lies in I_{s′_0}, and also in the kernel of I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0}. But under I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab it maps onto G^ab, as T is a maximal torus of G. So the map does not factor through I_{s_0} unless G^ab = 1. The same happens over Q_ℓ, so the justification "as this is true over Q_ℓ" fails too. Surjectivity of I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0} alone cannot give a factorization. What is needed is that the kernel maps trivially, and the fibre product above provides this. Lemma 2.2.8 is used in the proof of Proposition 2.2.2 (p.28). Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 7, item T23) as a descent gate; the analysis and the fibre-product repair are given here.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.2.11, p.29, in the author PDF https://math.berkeley.edu/~swshin/HT.pdf (41 pp., created 27 January 2021, SHA-256 fd22990b…52db), the latest version found; the published text, Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), 1559–1614, was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "Lemma 2.2.11. Let S be an irreducible scheme of finite type over a field k, and Γ ⊂ S(k) a Zariski dense subset. Let W ⊂ Aut_k S be a finite subgroup, and σ ∈ Aut_k S. Suppose that for every γ ∈ Γ, there exists w ∈ W such that w(γ) = σ(γ). Then σ = w for some w ∈ W."
sourceIssues.correction: Assume in addition that S is reduced and separated (for example a variety). Then two automorphisms that agree on a dense set of points agree, because their equalizer is a closed subscheme containing a dense set, and the proof applies.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof ends "Γ_{w_0} is dense in S … and it follows that σ = w_0". That step fails without reducedness or separatedness. For S = Spec k[ε]/ε² with char k ≠ 2, the automorphism ε ↦ 2ε fixes the unique point, which is dense; with W trivial it is a counterexample. For the affine line with doubled origin, the automorphism exchanging the two origins fixes the dense set of other k-points; again W is trivial. The lemma is applied on p.30 to a maximal torus T, which is reduced and separated, so nothing changes. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 4, item G16); the separatedness counterexample is added here.

sourceIssues.printed: "Let S be a flat, normal, finite type W-scheme, D ⊂ S a relative Cartier divisor, and j : U = D − S ↪ S, the inclusion. We consider S as a log scheme equipped with the log structure j_*O_U"
sourceIssues.correction: U = S − D, and S carries the divisorial log structure O_S ∩ j_*O_U^× → O_S.
sourceIssues.reason: D is a divisor in S, so the open complement is S − D; "D − S" is empty. The abelian scheme A is given over U and extends semi-abelianly over S, which also needs U = S − D. A log structure is a sheaf of monoids mapping to O_S. The sheaf of rings j_*O_U is not one; the intended one is the functions on S that are invertible on U. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 8, item A07).
